heroHeadline: Kennedy Center Board Restores Trump's Name, Closes Venue for 2 Years as Trump Orders Navy Back to Steam Catapults
heroSubtitle: On August 13, 2026 (Day 571), the Trump-appointed Kennedy Center board voted to inscribe 'Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump' on the venue's facade and name the surrounding grounds 'President Donald J. Trump Plaza,' while closing the main building until 2028 for a $250M renovation — three months after a federal judge ordered Trump's name removed, ruling only Congress could authorize a rename; Democratic board member Rep. Joyce Beatty called it 'a transparent effort to circumvent the Court's ruling.' The same day, US District Judge Emmet Sullivan pressed DOJ attorneys over Epstein-files redactions and warned of possible contempt. On August 14 (Day 572), Trump signed a national security memorandum ordering the Navy to abandon EMALS and revert to steam catapults on its newest Ford-class carriers, starting with USS Doris Miller — a switch the Navy and General Atomics warn will cost billions. This follows an active week: on Aug 11, Trump-backed Mike Lindell lost the Minnesota GOP governor primary to Lisa Demuth, and Trump declined to rule out declaring a 'national security emergency' over the midterms ('stranger things have happened') after the Senate again blocked his SAVE America Act; on Aug 10, Trump signed an executive order overhauling the childhood vaccine schedule, citing unsubstantiated autism claims and drawing pushback from Sen. Bill Cassidy. Trump's approval sits near 38% approve / 59% disapprove (net -20.6, YouGov/Economist), among the lowest of either term, with the July jobs report showing the first negative payrolls reading (-23,000) of his second term.
